fullPassage: It is natural for people to observe happenings and then seek explanations for why those happenings occurred. But sometimes the reasoning is wrong because of one or more misconceptions. One of these is the ecological fallacy, where an argument claims that there is a causal relationship between two things merely because they occur together. For example, in the 1950s it was found that crime rates were the highest in neighborhoods where immigrants were most numerous. Some people used this "co-occurrence" to argue that immigrants were a cause of crime. But a careful analysis of this situation revealed that immigrants were forced to live in neighborhoods where crime rates were already high; they could not afford more expensive housing in safer neighborhoods. Immigrants themselves committed very few of the crimes. Unless you analyze the claim carefully, you would misinterpret the relationship and thereby construct a faulty belief.

❌ ③ revealed: 과거시제 동사로 적절. 분석이 드러냈다
❌ ④ few: 가산명사 crimes와 함께 '거의 ~않은'을 뜻하는 few로 적절
det.tip: where = in which (관계부사, 선행사가 추상적 상황/경우일 때도 사용)

questions.passage: It is natural for people to observe happenings and then seek explanations for why those happenings occurred. But sometimes the reasoning is (A)[correct / wrong] because of one or more misconceptions. One of these is the ecological fallacy, where an argument claims that there is a causal relationship between two things merely because they occur together. For example, in the 1950s it was found that crime rates were the highest in neighborhoods where immigrants were most numerous. Some people used this "co-occurrence" to argue that immigrants were a cause of crime. But a careful analysis of this situation revealed that immigrants were (B)[forced / willing] to live in neighborhoods where crime rates were already high; they could not afford more expensive housing in safer neighborhoods. Immigrants themselves committed very few of the crimes. Unless you analyze the claim carefully, you would misinterpret the relationship and thereby (C)[construct / demolish] a faulty belief.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) wrong=잘못된, (B) forced=강요된, (C) construct=구성하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① wrong — forced — construct: 원문 일치. 추론이 잘못되고(wrong), 이민자들이 강요받아(forced) 살았으며, 결함 있는 믿음을 구성하게(construct) 된다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② correct — forced — construct: (A) correct(올바른)는 '오해 때문에 추론이 올바르다'가 되어 문맥과 모순
❌ ③ wrong — willing — construct: (B) willing(자발적인)은 forced(강요된)의 반대로, 이민자들이 자발적으로 살았다는 뜻이 되어 부적절
❌ ④ wrong — forced — demolish: (C) demolish(파괴하다)는 construct(구성하다)와 반대 의미로 부적절

(③) For example, in the 1950s it was found that crime rates were the highest in neighborhoods where immigrants were most numerous. Some people used this "co-occurrence" to argue that immigrants were a cause of crime. But a careful analysis of this situation revealed that immigrants were forced to live in neighborhoods where crime rates were already high; they could not afford more expensive housing in safer neighborhoods. (④) Immigrants themselves committed very few of the crimes. Unless you analyze the claim carefully, you would misinterpret the relationship and thereby construct a faulty belief.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? "In other words, the two facts were related but one did not cause the other."

det.korean: 즉, 두 사실은 관련이 있었지만 하나가 다른 하나를 야기한 것은 아니었다
det.analysis:
❌ ① 첫 문장 뒤: 아직 생태학적 오류나 구체적 사례가 언급되기 전이라 '두 사실'의 지시 대상이 없음
❌ ② 오해에 대한 일반론 뒤: 아직 구체적 사례가 나오지 않아 '두 사실이 관련되어 있었다'는 내용의 맥락이 부족
❌ ③ 생태학적 오류 정의 뒤: 아직 구체적 예시(이민자-범죄율)가 나오기 전이므로 부적절
✅ ④ 분석 결과(이민자들은 비싼 주거를 감당할 수 없었다) 뒤: 이민자 수와 범죄율이 함께 높았지만(related), 이민자가 범죄의 원인은 아니었다(one did not cause the other)는 요약으로 자연스러움 ←정답
det.tip: related but not causal = 관련되어 있지만 인과 관계는 아님
